minutes.headline: Capital planning committee reviewed the FY26 capital list with the new town manager; only minutes and adjournment were voted.
minutes.summary: The committee met at Town Hall with the new town manager to reconcile the FY26 capital plan list in the draft warrant article with its own ranking and the former interim manager's recommendation. Discussion covered the teen center floor, Marshall Pond weed treatment, a track and field warrant article outside the plan, and a special projects article with TC Passos decommissioning and cemetery road repairs. The only votes were approving two sets of minutes and adjourning.

public_comment.topic: Objected that discussing a town meeting warrant article is outside the committee's purview.
Said a non-resident should need a community sponsor to speak at public comment.
Opposed spending on the TC Passos roof since schools are vacating.
History of Marshall Pond and Wham Lake permitting delays, held up by the state.
Said the former manager's changes had no public discussion; opposed cemetery road money without a plan; supported fixing the track.
Asked for a consultant's opinion on life expectancy of Marshall Pond weed treatment; opposed pavement management money for cemeteries; asked about past abatement spending.
A member raised senior center parking and the lack of a conceptual layout (a board member, not public).

votes.motion: Approve minutes of December 16th and January 29th.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager questioned the flooring item given financial constraints; members defended it as a modest maintenance project, one wanting a revenue model.
Public purpose questioned; a member would drop it since it ranked low and the free cash is limited.
The manager said the plan is fully funded with reappropriated prior-year items and a debt service reduction.
Engineering to get the project bid ready; total project estimated near the stated figure; free cash for the schools discussed.

budget_items.topic: Special projects article (TC Passos, cemetery roads)
budget_items.what_was_said: Decommissioning and cemetery road repairs sit outside the capital plan, in lieu of a larger cemetery request.
A resident cited cemetery cost estimates and said patching money is a band-aid.

transfers.description: Reappropriation of two prior-year capital items (old Primary School hazardous waste abatement and PSB engineering design/drainage)

decisions.decision: Members agreed such meetings with the town manager should be held regularly before town meeting.
The chair forwarded the former interim manager's January recommendation to the town manager.

what_happened.line: The only votes were to approve two sets of minutes and to adjourn; no vote was taken on the FY26 capital list.
The committee went through the draft warrant article's FY26 capital list with the new town manager, who questioned the teen center flooring and Marshall Pond weed treatment.
The manager said the FY26 capital plan is fully funded through reappropriated prior-year items and a debt service reduction.
A track and field warrant article and a special projects article (TC Passos decommissioning, cemetery roads) sit outside the capital plan; the special projects item ended with no resolution.
Members agreed such meetings with the town manager should be held regularly before town meeting.

why_it_matters: The capital list that goes to town meeting is shaped partly by items this committee did not rank, such as the track and field and special projects articles, so what residents vote on can differ from the committee's own ranking.

Because the plan is described as funded by reappropriated prior-year items and a debt service reduction, the projects in it may not require new money, while the articles outside it are where new spending questions fall.
